reviewer: Independent Codex GATE: bounded offline pre-start continuation implementation
scope: Implementation acceptance only for the exact frozen continuation helper, cutover delta and new synthetic tests. Not a companion-prestart-continuation-v1 approval record, refreshed execution handoff or operational authorization.
shown: All three frozen code/test hashes match the requested review. In-memory removal of only the continuation import, paired CLI options, validation/recheck, execution-ID reservation and added receipt evidence reconstructs the exact previously reviewed fcea6d3e entrypoint bytes. Existing load_inputs, runtime/controller dispatch, success checks, publication, recovery and cleanup code are otherwise unchanged.

Absent both continuation options preserves the ordinary preparation-keyed one-shot path. Supplying only one refuses. No bare execution-ID override, automatic retry, preparation relabel/rebuild or marker cleanup is added.

The accepted continuation record is hash-bound, parsed with duplicate-key refusal and an exact key set. Schema/decision/reviewer, a valid distinct execution ID, unchanged manifest/preparation/review/runtime hashes, exact ordered four prepared IDs, prior-receipt digest and exact ten-consumer hash map are validated before reservation or token consumption.

The prior receipt is opened under the configured root through directory descriptors with O_DIRECTORY/O_NOFOLLOW and owner/non-writable-by-others checks. The fixed receipt.jsonl file uses O_NOFOLLOW/O_NONBLOCK, must be regular, same-owner and exactly0600, and is bounded to64KiB. No arbitrary prior-receipt path comes from the approval record.

Receipt eligibility requires its trusted exact hash and exactly four complete canonical records: inputs bound, installation reserved with the specified startup/network contract, staged_checks intended, and staged_preflight failure. Canonical comparison distinguishes boolean values from numeric impostors and rejects altered/additional/truncated evidence.

The optional record, current consumer hashes and prior receipt are revalidated after acquisition of the existing shared nonblocking lock and before new reservation/token consumption. A changed record/receipt or busy lock refuses without dispatch in the synthetic tests.

A separate execution ID selects only the new receipt directory. _reserve still uses exclusive creation and refuses an existing final directory, including a symlink. Partial reservation/fsync failure remains consumed. The original preparation attempt, prior receipt, labels/names and prepared IDs are not changed.

The new initial receipt binds execution ID, preparation attempt, continuation-review digest and prior-receipt digest alongside unchanged input bindings. Token consumption remains after recheck, successful reservation and initial receipt creation.

The same reviewed plan and prepared object reach the existing Installer.run path. Its fresh staged preflight, same-ID checks, storage preservation,600second controller budget/180second recovery reserve, one archived query and owned rollback are not weakened or bypassed.

The new tests independently pass with native/network paths forbidden and fixture-only token/native/runtime state. Synthetic success preserves the same four IDs, starts four application fixtures and invokes one explanation; reuse of that execution ID refuses before consuming another fixture token. Publication failure exercises existing owned rollback and preserves the prior receipt.

reviewed_boundaries.fail_closed: Malformed, unaccepted, hash-changed, duplicate-key, mixed-option, source-drift, wrong-binding or ineligible-prior evidence refuses before dispatch. Unexpected validation exceptions are caught by existing main and cannot enable execution.
reviewed_boundaries.replay: Exclusive receipt reservation prevents reuse of the same execution ID. A different execution ID requires a different independently trusted accepted record and separate authorization; the implementation does not manufacture that record or infer permission from a prior failure.
reviewed_boundaries.token_ordering: The consumer rechecks and reserves before token_from_pipe. This does not approve or implement a producer; any future token handoff must be separately reviewed and preserve its own ordering/secret handling.
reviewed_boundaries.same_IDs: Exact ordered replacement IDs remain bound to the unchanged reviewed preparation/runtime inputs. Fresh fixture drift in an original or replacement is refused before lifecycle dispatch.
reviewed_boundaries.paths_and_lock: Directory traversal is excluded by the execution-ID grammar; receipt traversal is anchored to fixed parts and validated plan attempt. Symlinks/private-mode violations and busy shared lock are refused. This assumes ordinary trusted-owner filesystem/lock cooperation, not protection from a malicious same-user writer ignoring the lock.
reviewed_boundaries.rollback: The existing controller/wrapper recovery logic is reused unchanged. A synthetic publication-failure case confirms one owned rollback and original-state restoration; no actual rollback or native success is established.

Receipt/path checks and under-lock revalidation are not a forensic filesystem snapshot or a defense against arbitrary same-owner writes after validation. No stronger immutability claim follows.
